description: Machine-readable encoding & crypto vectors mirrored from zh/conformance/conformance-vectors.md §1.3-§1.13. Conformance runners MUST execute every vector and compare canonical_bytes / digest / order outputs. The crypto.ed25519_detached_jws vector lives separately in crypto-signature-fixture.json; the rank_order vector covers hex-Base32 rank string ordering (LIST item placement).
generator_semantics: Vectors of kind *_reject_generated carry a `generator` object instead of literal input bytes: the runner MUST construct the input at execution time from the generator parameters (e.g. nesting_depth, array_item_count) following the generator.rule text, so the fixture never stores megabyte-scale literals. Rejection is asserted exactly as for literal-input vectors.

rules: an unknown value from an open registry MUST NOT fail deserialization of the containing object
the exact unknown string MUST survive decode and encode
admission may still return unsupported_event_kind or another profile-defined result after parsing
schema-declared x_* and critical extension parameter slots are canonical signed content
unknown nested values MUST be preserved without key filtering, normalization, or reordering beyond canonical encoding
a receiver that does not implement the optional extension still preserves and forwards its exact content
object key MUST be sorted by UTF-16 code unit at every level
array order MUST be preserved as input
string values MUST NOT be rewritten by key sort
hash the exact UTF-8 bytes recorded by expected_input_hex without a trailing newline or Unicode normalization
the digest prefix, lowercase hex length, and Realm digest_algorithm are part of the verified suite contract
implementations declaring ak.profile.hash.blake3.v1 MUST pass the positive KAT and every negative case
NaN / Infinity / -Infinity MUST reject
-0 MUST reject
v1 signed JSON numbers MUST be integers; 1.0 / 1e0 / fractional or exponent decimal spellings MUST reject instead of being canonicalised
signature verification MUST run only after canonicalisation succeeds

rejected_input_categories: duplicate JSON object keys at the same level
lone surrogate or ambiguous escape sequence
non-integer JSON numbers or parser-accepted numbers that cannot be proven to be integers
rules: duplicate keys MUST NOT be silently overwritten by parser default
malformed strings MUST NOT be replaced with U+FFFD before signing
rejection MUST be auditable; reason_code SHOULD be schema_violation, invalid_canonical_json, or invalid_encoding
event digest MUST be derived from canonical bytes after stripping proofs and unsigned, before redaction
event_id MUST appear inside the digest input but does not replace the digest
transport envelope, HTTP headers, sync metadata, and local receive time MUST NOT be hashed
the same event MUST yield the same digest on every Events API and Principal Server sync surface

fail_conditions: producer hashes events before canonical set normalization
receiver accepts an unsorted or duplicate signed wire events array
proof field included in receipt digest

rules: proof MUST bind event_digest, actor DID, verification_method, and created_at
cross-service / cross-domain verification SHOULD additionally bind domain or audience
actual ed25519 detached JWS for this binding lives in crypto-signature-fixture.json
HLC MUST sort by (unix_ms, logical, node_id_hash)
implementations MUST NOT compare HLC as raw wall-clock string unless the profile guarantees fixed-width lowercase hex such that string compare equals tuple compare

expected_acceptable_outcomes: wait until unix_ms_hex advances, then emit 01970e589d22-0000-a13f9c2e
return local error hlc_logical_overflow before canonical bytes are produced; caller retries
fail_conditions: logical counter wraps to a smaller value while still emitting events
wall-clock skew is forged to escape overflow at the cost of HLC monotonicity or causality
consumer accepts wrap-around values into accepted history

vectors.fixture_freshness_note: Timestamps are fixed at year 2099 deliberately so the static vector cannot expire during normal spec lifetime. Implementations generating their own conformance cursors MUST use fresh `issued_at`/`expires_at` matching their authority's clock; do NOT reuse this fixture's timestamps on the wire.
client_rules: MUST treat cursor as an opaque string and round-trip it verbatim
MUST NOT parse v / purpose / issued_at / expires_at / h to construct the next page request
MUST handle cursor decode failure by treating cursor as opaque, not by aborting the protocol
server_rules: MUST validate v, purpose, issued_at, expires_at, the full core cursor schema, and h handle binding before honouring cursor
syntax validation failure MUST return param_invalid with reason_code invalid_cursor; TTL failure MUST return cursor_expired; handle lookup or binding failure MUST return cursor_integrity_invalid
fail_conditions: client parses h/expiry and rebuilds a request
core server accepts a cursor body without h

rules: payload_metadata is exactly {version,content_type,encryption_context}; scope, kind, group id, scheme and sender domain are reconstructed and never duplicated on wire
standard MLS encryption_context omits counter; exporter encryption_context requires the full-width counter and is cross-checked against the exact group-state scheme
implementations MUST NOT hash plaintext payload
UTF-16 code-unit ordering places the supplementary-plane key before U+FFFF because its high surrogate 0xD83D sorts before 0xFFFF.
duplicate JSON object keys at the same level MUST reject before canonicalisation
non-NFC string input MUST reject before signature verification
U+FEFF / UTF-8 BOM injection MUST reject
malformed HLC strings MUST reject

generator.rule: runner builds a JSON object nested 65 levels deep, e.g. {"a":{"a":{...{"a":1}...}}} where the top-level container counts as depth 1; a mixed object/array variant of the same depth MUST also reject

rules: canonical JSON / deterministic CBOR structure nesting depth MUST NOT exceed 64 (objects and arrays combined, top-level container = depth 1); see zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md section 2
receiver MUST fail bounded before recursive descent can exhaust the stack (depth-bounded recursion or explicit worklist)
a control input of depth exactly 64 MUST be accepted (the limit is inclusive)
byte string header (0x5a, 4-byte length) declares 4294967295 bytes but only 4 bytes of input remain; declared length MUST be <= remaining input
decoder MUST reject before allocating any buffer sized from the declared length (capacity-bomb resistance)
applies to every hand-written deterministic CBOR structure, including the mls_governance_binding GroupContext extension
input is the indefinite-length map {_ "a": 1} (0xbf ... 0xff); indefinite-length items (map 0xbf, array 0x9f, string 0x5f/0x7f) violate RFC 8949 section 4.2 deterministic encoding and MUST reject
receiver MUST NOT normalise indefinite-length items into definite-length form and continue
applies to every hand-written deterministic CBOR structure, including the mls_governance_binding GroupContext extension

generator.rule: runner emits a definite-length CBOR array header declaring 65537 items followed by 65537 encodings of unsigned integer 0

rules: a single array or map in a hand-written deterministic CBOR structure MUST NOT declare or contain more than 65536 items; see zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md section 2
decoder MUST NOT preallocate item storage from the declared count before the bound check

vectors.description: Golden vectors for the base58btc multibase encoding of Ed25519 public keys with the 0xed01 multicodec prefix and the resulting did:key identifier. Generated and round-trip verified (encode -> decode) by the reference implementation.
rules: multibase encoding MUST be base58btc with the leading 'z' prefix (multibase table)
the multicodec prefix for Ed25519 public keys MUST be the varint 0xed01, prepended to the 32 raw public key bytes before base58btc encoding

decode MUST round-trip to the original 32 public key bytes; a multibase string whose decoded payload is not exactly 34 bytes (2-byte multicodec prefix + 32 key bytes) or whose prefix is not 0xed01 MUST be rejected
did:key identifiers embed the multibase string verbatim: did:key:<multibase>
base binding fields follow ak.vector.encoding.signature_binding_payload.v1 (event_digest, actor DID, verification_method, created_at)
cross-domain verification binds the target service domain via the optional domain field; the canonical bytes sort it between created_at and event_digest
absent optional fields MUST be omitted from the canonical binding object entirely; a null placeholder changes the canonical bytes and MUST NOT be emitted
base binding fields follow ak.vector.encoding.signature_binding_payload.v1 (event_digest, actor DID, verification_method, created_at)
audience-constrained verification binds a single audience DID via the optional audience field
absent optional fields MUST be omitted from the canonical binding object entirely; a null placeholder changes the canonical bytes and MUST NOT be emitted
base binding fields follow ak.vector.encoding.signature_binding_payload.v1 (event_digest, actor DID, verification_method, created_at)
domain and audience MAY be combined; audience MAY be an array of DIDs whose order is preserved verbatim in the canonical bytes
absent optional fields MUST be omitted from the canonical binding object entirely; a null placeholder changes the canonical bytes and MUST NOT be emitted
resolve every participant identifier to its stable subject DID before constructing the input; an unresolved pairwise DID fails closed
sort the two normalized stable subject DIDs by unsigned UTF-8 byte order before constructing participants

canonicalize exactly {participants:[p0,p1],trust_domain_id:realm_trust_domain_id} with JCS and compute SHA-256 over UTF8(ak.direct-conversation.pair-key.v1 followed by LF) concatenated with those canonical bytes; the resulting sha256:<lowercase-hex> value is pair_key
reversing the caller-supplied participant order MUST yield the same pair_key after the required sort
binding_digest is receiver-derived and MUST NOT appear in direct_conversation_bound_payload
sort participants_unordered and authorization_basis.event_refs by unsigned UTF-8 bytes before constructing the closed binding object
created_at and Event author/proof are absent from the binding object and therefore cannot affect the digest
the core OR-Set tag remains the canonical Event dot; (binding_digest, actor_id) is the domain-view endorsement identity only

vectors.subject: ak:did_core:web:subject.example
rules: the scope-set component and outer composite subject always use SHA-256 and base64url without padding
sorting compares raw UTF-8 bytes after JSON decoding and performs no text normalization
active and revoked payloads with the same exact set derive the same cell
a subset revoke addresses only the subset cell and never mutates a superset cell

vectors.description: Producer-biased canonical presentation and serialization order. Decoded digest octets sort ascending, with canonical suite id as secondary key only when octets are identical. The order never selects a semantic winner or removes a candidate.

cases.name: cross_suite_prefix_order_opposes_decoded_octet_order
cases.description: The suite prefix string order and the decoded octet order disagree on purpose. Comparing the whole typed wire string as UTF-8 selects the wrong winner.

cases.name: same_typed_digest_different_preimage_fails_closed
cases.injection: lattice_test_seam_only; MUST NOT register a fake active hash suite or forge a real SHA-256 collision

vectors.description: Canonical OR-Set dot and or_set_batch_add tag encoding. dot = "ak:event:" + event_id + ":" + write_index, where write_index is the 0-based index of the write in the event kind's registry cell_writes[]. batch_tag = base64url_nopad(sha256(utf8(tag_context) || 0x0A || utf8(dot) || 0x0A || canonical_json(values[i]))) over values sorted by canonical value ascending.

negative_cases.name: bare_event_id_as_tag
negative_cases.note: A bare event_id is not a dot; it is not unique across multiple or_set writes on one cell.

negative_cases.name: wire_array_index_as_third_segment
negative_cases.note: The third segment MUST be the registry cell_writes[] index; v1 has no producer-written effect array.

rules: the registry cell_subject.kind selects the embedding rule; uri percent-encodes every octet outside ALPHA / DIGIT / - . _ ~ with upper-case hex, including : / and % itself
encoding % is what keeps the transform injective: a segment carrying %2F and a path carrying a real / are two different rooms and MUST NOT fold onto one cell
the transform addresses a cell and never normalizes one: a non-canonical mimi_room_uri MUST be rejected with schema_violation before any subject is derived
